2. The facts in short are that one Syed Mozammel Hossain was the owner of 181/2 decimals of land in C.S. and S.A. Plot no. 841 and one decimal in C.S. and S.A. Plot No. 843. He transferred .0668 acres of land to one Rabeya Khatun by two registered deeds dated 24.10.1987 and 26.10.1987. After purchase, the said Rabeya Khatun mutated her name in respect of the aforesaid lands. She transferred the said land to the appellant- pre-emptor by a registered deed of Heba bel Ewaj on 28.1.1991. The aforesaid Syed Mozammel Hossain, respondent no. 2, subsequently transferred another piece of land measuring 0.0878 acre, the case-land, in favour of one Khaleda Rahman, pre-emptee-respondent no. 1, by a registered deed of sale dated 8.6.1991, without any notice to the appellant petitioner. The petitioner in due course, came to know about the transfer and thereafter filed a pre-emption case being Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 80 of 1991 under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949, contending inter alia, that the purchaser respondent no.1 is a stranger to the case-land while he is a co-sharer. The purchaser respondent no.1 (preempted) contested the miscellaneous case contending inter alia that the case land was sold in her favour and that neither the pre-emptor nor his mother is a co-sharer in the case land , as such, he has got no right to pre-empt the case land. 

 6. Leave was granted to consider firstly, as to whether the alleged mutation in the name of the petitioner's mother was actually made by a competent authority in accordance with the provision of section 117(1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the payment of rents in separate jama was proper, that as to whether the appellant's mother ceased to be a co-sharer, secondly, as to whether the findings arrived at in the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 5 of 1994, act as resjudicata in respect of the issues involved in the Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 80 of 1991. 

 7. Mr. T.H. Khan, Senior Advocate, appears on behalf of the appellant (pre-emptor). He submits that the judgment of the Trial Court below in refusing the pre-emption, was passed on an erroneous finding that Rabeya Khatun, the mother of the petitioner, mutated her name and separated the jama, but as a matter of fact no such separation of jama was made in accordance with the provisions of section 117 (1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, after notifying all the other co-sharers but mutated her name only in order to deposit the ground rent to the revenue authority in respect of her purchased land, rather, this mutation and the alleged separation of jama was made illegally and has got no relevance in a pre-emption proceeding. When confronting with the admission of the pre-emptor as to the mutation and payment of rent on the basis of a separation of jama by mother, the learned Advocate submits that this was a bonafide mistake of fact and not supported by any evidence on record; as such, Rabeya Khatun the mother of the pre-emptor never ceased to be a co-sharer in the jama as was erroneously found by the trial Court. He further submits that during the pendency of the pre-emption case, the pre-emptee filed a title suit praying for a decree for declaration that the deed of heba bel ewaj executed and registered by Rabeya Khatun in favour of her son, was null and void and that the pre-emptor and his vendor are not co-sharers in the case-land. But his suit was dismissed by the trial Court which was affirmed upto the Appellate Division. In this respect, the learned Advocate submits that the findings arrived at in the said suit on contest, act as resjudicata in the issues involved so far the co-sharership of the appellant and his mother is concerned, as such, he submits that the High Court Division wrongly and erroneously made the Rule absolute and upheld the order of rejection of the prayer for pre-emption by the trial Court. 

 12. On appeal, the learned Additional District Judge, held that Rabey'a Khatun although separated her jama and mutated her name in respect of the case land but as a matter of fact, did not cease to be a co-sharer therein. The learned Judge based his findings, firstly, on the ground that had she ceased to be a co-sharer then the pre-emptee would not have filed a separate suit. Besides, he found that the said separate jama was only for the purpose of payment of ground rent to the revenue authority and nothing more. The High Court Division in civil revision however, found that admittedly the pre-emptor's mother having mutated her name, paid rents in respect of the case-land. The pre-emptor himself filed the mutation khatian which was marked 'X' and it is clear from the said mutation khatian that his mother mutated her name after purchase of 0.0660 acres of land and a new khatian being No. 732/7-1 was opened in her name as far back as in the year 1987 whereas the kabala under pre-emption is dated 8.6.1991. The learned Judge of the High Court Division also noticed that after separation of the khatian the pre-emptor's mother paid rent separately and thus the order of mutation has been given effect to and acted upon. As such, the learned Judge held that no question of irregularity arose in separating the case-land by a separate khatian within the meaning of section 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and accordingly, the question of pre-emption does not arise. 

 14. It appears that it is specifically stated at paragraph-1 of the petition of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 80 of 1991 as follows: 

 15. Besides, in paragraph 3 of the petition it is stated: 

 16. The mutation khatian prepared by the Tahsilder was produced in Court and was marked 'X'. This was produced at the instance of the pre-emptor himself. In his examination-in-chief, he stated as follows: 

 17. On perusal of the Khatian No. 732/7-1, it appears that the case land was recorded in the name of Mrs. Rabeya Khatun in pursuance of the Mutation Case No. 19455 of 1987 dated 17.11.1987 signed by the Tahsilder on 21.12.1987(Marked-X). It appears from those statements and documents that the High Court Division rightly found that there was a proper separation of jama and mutation was effected in favour of Mrs. Rabeya Khatun, mother of the pre-emptor. So far the contention that the findings of the Court in Title Suit No. 5 of 1994, is binding upon the learned Assistant Judge, in disposing of the Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 80 of 1991 is concerned, we have gone through the judgment passed by the trial Court, the appellate Court, the judgment passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 600 of 1991 dated 19.5.1997 and also The Lawyers the judgment of dismissal of Leave Petition No. 714 of 1997 arising therefrom and passed by the Appellate Division on 12.11.1997.
